question: How should stored data be migrated when a Soroban contract upgrade changes its data structures?

golden.answer: Updating a contract's Wasm keeps the contract address and storage; it does not rewrite stored values into a new schema. As of 2026-11-02, contracts built with soroban-sdk v28+ (Protocol 28, CAP-86) read named-field `#[contracttype]` structs sparsely: an added `Option` field reads as `None` and a removed field is ignored, so only those changes can skip migration. Version stored records and use either lazy migration on read/write or a controlled migration entrypoint that converts bounded batches. Keep old and new decoding paths only for the migration window, make the operation idempotent, test against production-shaped state, and retain rollback or pause controls. Large migrations should be batched to stay within transaction resources.
keyFacts: A Wasm upgrade does not automatically transform existing contract storage.
Versioned records support lazy migration or a controlled explicit entrypoint.
Large migrations should be idempotent and batched to fit transaction resource limits.
avoid: Uploading new Wasm automatically re-encodes all existing storage values.
Every migration must fit into one transaction.
golden.notes: As of 2026-11-02: CAP-86 sparse unpacking applies only to contracts rebuilt with soroban-sdk v28+. Non-Option field additions, type changes, enums, and tuple structs still need migration. Recommending versioned records for every schema change remains correct. The official migrate-contract-storage guide still says reading a stored DataV1 as a DataV2 with an added Option field traps with Error(Object, UnexpectedSize), with no SDK-version scope (observed 2026-11-02; improvements/stellar-docs/sd-070-migrate-contract-storage-cap-86-scope.md). That trap claim is correct for pre-v28 builds, and a v28+ read still errors on a missing non-Option field. It is wrong only when the answer says that, on a v28+ build, an added Option field or a removed field of a named-field struct traps.
